4.place: In the quiet before you become what you already are
4.ask: Take the next step actually under your feet, with the little light you have. Don't plan the one after it; when this step is done, more ground tends to show.
4.core:
You are moving faster than you are choosing. Decisions are getting made — something keeps getting done — but not by you in the moment they happen; the reaction arrives and you are already past it. Doors you could not see are not locked. They were not in the picture.

Not every path needs seeing first. Take the next step actually under your feet and do only that one, with the little bit of light you have. Do not plan the step after it. When that one is done, the ground ahead tends to show a little more. You can steer once you can see, and you see by moving.
4.sheetLine: You can steer only what you can see, and you see by moving.

1.tense: You are here, in the open moment before anything has to be decided.
1.verb: being everything you could still become, not yet decided
1.place: a place where you look at the whole shape of what's in front of you from inside it
1.ask: From what you're holding right now, pick the one you'd miss most if it went, and hold that in view a moment. Leave the rest as they are.
1.core:
You can stand in front of everything you haven't decided yet and not force any of them into a shape. That's rarer than it sounds. From inside a situation you can still see its whole outline — where you are in it, what it's made of — and you don't use that to judge anyone. You just recognise. People feel known around you without being weighed.

From what you're holding right now, pick the one you'd miss most if it went. Hold it in view a moment. Nothing else moves; the rest can stay exactly as they are. Having one thing quietly leading the others changes how the deciding goes — it stops being a negotiation with everything at once. That's all this is. Just let the first thing be first.
1.sheetLine: One thing leads the others now, quietly, and the rest can wait.

2.tense: You will keep every door open, and so none of them will let you through.
2.verb: being everything you could still become, not yet decided
2.place: a place where you look at the whole shape of what's in front of you from inside it
2.ask: Finish something already underway your own way this week — not the polished version. When it's done, don't explain or justify it to anyone.
2.core:
You can see how every option could still turn out well, so you hold all of them open, and none gets to become anything. Each stays a size larger than the last, softer, so nothing settles into a life that would need living on a schedule. From the inside it feels like staying ready. From outside it reads like nothing has been given the chance to land.

There's another half to this. Finish something already underway the way you alone would finish it. Not the version you'd show someone to prove it. Yours, and no explanation afterward. One piece of work done plainly as itself gives the whole field something to land on. You don't have to settle everything. Just let this one be what it is.
2.sheetLine: Everything stays possible because nothing has settled into a shape.

3.tense: You are still standing at a door that is already behind you.
3.verb: being everything you could still become, not yet decided
3.place: a place where you look at the whole shape of what's in front of you from inside it
3.ask: Stay with something you're already carrying, longer than you'd normally stay — past where you'd usually turn away. Notice what it shows you that you didn't have before.
3.core:
You can usually see the whole shape of a situation from the inside, and a while back that closed. You read from a distance now, aimed at what's already settled. You work from what you know rather than from what's around you. It isn't blindness. It's a shorter leash on looking, and it was probably a sensible one to take.

Stay with something you're already carrying, longer than you'd normally stay. Not a new thing — the same one, seen past where you'd usually turn away. What it shows you will be old ground not yet finished. Nothing has to open today. Looking at the same thing more deeply is how the whole shape comes back.
3.sheetLine: You see the shape — from further away, aimed at what's already fixed.

4.tense: You are already writing in a room whose doors you cannot see.
4.verb: being everything you could still become, not yet decided
4.place: a place where you look at the whole shape of what's in front of you from inside it
4.ask: Put something that's been sitting with you onto a single page, roughly — where you are in it, who's with you, what's around. Keep the page when you're done.
4.core:
You read situations fast, see the whole shape, and move on it before anyone's done explaining. You wouldn't call that seeing. You'd call it reacting, or being practical, or getting along. The recognition is happening; your name isn't on it. So the choices feel like things that happen to you, and the ways through don't look like ways through.

Put something that's been sitting with you onto a single page. Roughly. Where you are in it, who else is in it, what's around it. Keep the page afterward. It doesn't have to be accurate. You want the arrangement you're standing inside to have a line or two you can look at, so the next turn can be told apart from a wall.
4.sheetLine: You read the room and call it reacting.

1.tense: Today you arrive with no plan, and that openness is the whole engine of the moment.
1.verb: holding every possibility open before choosing one
1.place: the point where a thing is finished enough to hand on
1.ask: Take a small step toward something you actually want, and keep it to yourself unless you decide otherwise.
1.core:
You come to a fresh thing with nothing already decided — no plan, no exit picked, just open to what shows up. That isn't naivety. It's the beat before a choice collapses everything into one shape, and it's where your work begins. Where this holds steady, something gets finished and handed on without clutching: a piece goes out the door and you're facing the next one.

The bend is that open is so comfortable you can stay in it long past the moment it wants to become something. So take one small step toward what you actually want, at your own pace. No announcement, no armour on it. Not because wanting is the goal — because a thing chosen is the only thing that can finish, and finishing is what opens the next door for you.
1.sheetLine: Open is where you start, not where you live.

2.tense: Every door is still open, and you are hovering above all of them at once.
2.verb: holding every possibility open before choosing one
2.place: the point where a thing is finished enough to hand on
2.ask: Do something already waiting on your attention your own way today, and skip explaining how you did it.
2.core:
You can hold every version of a thing at once — all the ways it could go, all the shapes it might take. From the outside it reads as someone standing at the threshold of everything, and nothing has landed. There's one more possibility worth keeping alive, one more version not ruled out, and holding them both has become the work.

What's underneath is that landing would mean being one thing instead of all of them. So take something already waiting on your attention and do it in your own manner. No explaining the method, no defending it, no checking whether it landed right. A thing done that way was going to be done that way regardless. Nothing gets proven. It just shows, and showing is the point.
2.sheetLine: All the doors are open, and none has been walked through.

3.tense: The opening that was once here is sealed, and you are making things from inside the shut room.
3.verb: holding every possibility open before choosing one
3.place: the point where a thing is finished enough to hand on
3.ask: Put the situation you're inside on one page, and mark where you stand in it.
3.core:
The place where a thing gets finished enough to hand on is still here, but it isn't being reached from where you are. What comes out of your hands now comes out narrow — the first version that fits, the one that gets past whatever is in the way.

You don't need to force anything open, and pushing feeling at it won't help. Instead look at the whole thing you're inside of, longer than you usually would, until you can see its edges. Put the arrangement on one page, with yourself on it. You don't have to fix the pattern. Marking where you stand is what reopens the floor under you.
3.sheetLine: The door shut, and you stopped noticing it.

4.tense: You are steering with no hand on the wheel, and the doors beside you keep going unseen.
4.verb: holding every possibility open before choosing one
4.place: the point where a thing is finished enough to hand on
4.ask: Catch one decision you made today without noticing it, then make the next one a yes or no you actually gave.
4.core:
The finishing-and-handing-on is happening — things get done, doors get walked through — and in your own telling of it, you aren't the one doing it. Reactions come out as if they were events. Options right there get read as the way things are. The deciding is real, it just isn't landing anywhere you'd claim.

You don't need to see the whole road to take the next step. Start smaller than the question: one decision you made today without noticing you made it. Don't analyse it, just see it. Then make the next one in the open, whether it comes out yes or no. You're not forcing clarity on fog. You're letting enough light land on one step to call it yours.
4.sheetLine: The doors are there, and you're not seen walking through them.
